title: [19/9/2021] - Australian men and women in different age groups who did regular physical activity in 2010
prompt: The bar chart below shows the percentage of Australian men and women in different age groups who did regular physical activity in 2010. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart gives information about the proportion of Australians engaging in frequent exercise, divided by their gender and age, in 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, it is clear that nearly half of the population engaged regularly in physical activities, regardless of their sex. Females also tended to do so more frequently than their male counterparts in their middle-aged years.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: The youngest group, from 15 to 24 years old, is the only age bracket in which men exercised more than women, with respective figures of 52.8% and 47.7%. In contrast, the country recorded the same emphasis on exercise for the retirement age group, where around 47% of the population took part in physical activities.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: For the remaining age groups, in their mid-20s to mid-30s, around 7% more females frequently did exercise than males, at 48.9% and 42.2%, respectively. As they got older, men were inclined to exercise more, with the figure of 45.1% in the 55-to-64-year-old bracket, while the corresponding figures for females, despite being higher, remained stable, at around 53%.
